en.headline: Chan says Hong Kong remains optimistic on growth after IMF upgrades forecast to 3.8 per…
en.dek: The Financial Secretary, writing after the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, noted the city’s unique position amid AI disruption and global energy price pressures.
body: Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said Hong Kong is more optimistic about its economic growth this year than the International Monetary Fund is about the global outlook, citing the city’s role in channelling international capital and supporting the artificial intelligence boom.

Writing on his blog on Sunday after attending the IMF and World Bank Group annual meetings in Bangkok, Chan said discussions among world leaders had been dominated by rapid disruption from AI and energy price surges linked to conflicts in the Middle East.

He noted that the IMF expected global growth to slow from 3.5 per cent last year to 3.1 per cent this year, while Asia would continue to expand at a faster pace. The IMF recently upgraded its 2026 real GDP growth forecast for Hong Kong to 3.8 per cent, from a previous projection of 2.4 per cent. The Hong Kong government has maintained its full-year forecast at 3.5 to 4.5 per cent.
Chan said the city is well placed to channel global capital, support mainland Chinese firms expanding overseas, and fund AI infrastructure in developing economies.

zh.headline: 陳茂波指香港對增長仍樂觀 IMF上調預測至3.8%仍保持政府區間
zh.dek: 財政司司長出席曼谷IMF年會後在博客指，全球受AI擾亂及中東衝突能源價格壓力影響，香港具獨特橋梁優勢。
body: 財政司司長陳茂波表示，香港對今年經濟增長的看法比國際貨幣基金組織對全球前景更樂觀，指本港在導入國際資本及支持人工智能發展方面具獨特優勢。
陳茂波星期日在博客撰文，回顧上周出席曼谷國際貨幣基金組織及世界銀行年會，指各國領導人討論主要圍繞人工智能帶來的急速擾亂，以及中東衝突導致的能源價格上升。
他指，IMF預計全球增長由去年3.5%放緩至今年3.1%，亞洲則繼續以較快步伐擴張。IMF最近將香港2026年實質本地生產總值增長預測由2.4%上調至3.8%。香港政府仍維持全年增長預測在3.5至4.5%區間。
陳茂波指，香港有條件導入全球資本、支持內地企業出海，以及為發展中經濟體的AI基建提供融資。
